utility.notes: Light and Power is the City of Fort Collins' electric utility, and the City's solar pages call the utility Fort Collins Utilities. Light and Power says it provides power to homes, businesses, schools and more across the city. When you check your own address, note that under the Municipal Code (Sec. 26-447) a property annexed to the City may keep receiving electric service from the utility that served it before, until the City elects to provide the service. The code also sets a service rights fee for areas annexed after April 22, 1989 that were previously served by Poudre Valley Rural Electric Association (PVREA). The City's pages do not list the addresses this affects, so check the utility named on your electric bill or use the Service Area Map linked on the Light and Power page.

value.name: Fort Collins Utilities
value.notes: Light and Power says it is part of Platte River Power Authority, which supplies power to four cities in Northern Colorado. Under net metering, energy returned to the grid is credited at the Time of Day rate in effect when it was returned, and unused credits roll over to the next month.

county.notes: The City pages reviewed do not name the county in a sentence. The City's Building Permits page tells applicants replacing a water heater in a commercial food service establishment to also contact the Larimer County Health Department.

permit_authority.value: City of Fort Collins Building Services
permit_authority.notes: Building Services reviews building plans, issues permits, performs inspections and licenses contractors for construction in Fort Collins. The office is at 281 N. College Ave., Fort Collins, CO 80524, and its listed hours are Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. To check whether a property is inside city limits, use the map linked on the Building Services page under "Is my property in the City of Fort Collins' limits?". Fire permits are managed by Poudre Fire Authority. The solar sections of the City's Building Permits page give no review or processing time.

permit_url.notes: The page lists three solar permit types under Exterior Permits: Solar PV (New Installation), Solar PV Reinstallation, and Solar PV Energy Storage System (ESS). Each solar section says to email the application to buildingservices@fortcollins.gov.

interconnection_url.notes: All interconnection applications go through PowerClerk, Fort Collins Utilities' online application platform. Your contractor submits the application paperwork on your behalf. Contractors are told to submit a building permit and a Utilities interconnection application for each solar or battery system, and the City's permit page says the Utilities Interconnect and Rebate Application must be submitted separately. The City describes the Permit to Operate as an official document that recognizes the system is fully operable and connected to the grid. If you plan to add panels to an existing system, the utility asks you to contact it before you talk to contractors, so it can check how much solar you may add under its size limits.

value.name: 2026 Battery Storage Incentive
value.description: $300 per kWh of battery capacity, up to a maximum incentive of $6,000. The minimum size is 6 kWh, and 20 kWh of usable battery capacity earns the maximum. Incentives are only available for new battery system installations. A battery can be added to an existing solar PV system, installed with a new one, or installed with no solar PV system. A battery-only project also needs a Distributed Energy Interconnection Application, submitted to the utility through PowerClerk. The incentive table is labeled 2026 and prints no end date.
value.eligibility: The system must be sold and installed by a Participating Solar Contractor. It must be interconnected behind a residential solar meter on the Fort Collins Utilities electric distribution network. The battery system must stay connected to the internet. It must be programmed either to store surplus solar energy to meet site loads or to follow the Time-of-Day rate structure.

required_documents.notes: Lists are as printed in the solar sections of the City's Building Permits page. The utility interconnection application is separate: for it, the contractor uploads documents in PowerClerk, including an electrical system design diagram, a site diagram showing all equipment locations and equipment spec sheets.

value: Your contractor starts the interconnection application in PowerClerk. The utility says not to begin installation before approval.
Get the building permit issued by Building Services.
Schedule the final inspection with Building Services, which inspects for electrical code compliance.
After the inspection passes, notify Utilities through PowerClerk.
Fort Collins Utilities inspects and tests the system (Utilities Testing).
After the system passes Utilities Testing, a Permit to Operate (PTO) is emailed to the customer and the contractor.
inspection_steps.notes: Steps follow the Step-by-Step Project Process on the Fort Collins Utilities Solar Contractor Resources page. The building permit, the Building Services final inspection and the utility's Permit to Operate are three separate approvals. The sources listed here do not say which inspection types to request for a solar permit, so ask Building Services when you schedule. The utility's pages give a six-month installation deadline but count it from different points (permit approval, project approval, or the rebate reservation letter). Confirm your deadline with the Utilities solar team.

timeline_days.notes: The solar sections of the City's Building Permits page give no review or processing time.

value.program_or_pathway: Solar PV permit, applied for by email to Building Services
other_conditions: Solar permits are listed under Exterior Permits, not under Fast-Track Permits, and the City's permit page describes no expedited or same-day path for solar.
The City's permit page notes that new building codes are in effect as of April 1, 2026.
For a new installation, the City asks for structural engineering and engineered electrical drawings stamped and signed by a Colorado-licensed engineer. The page gives no size threshold.
The City's page says a separate permit is required from Poudre Fire Authority for a new solar installation, with no residential or commercial qualifier.
If a homeowner does the work, the application must include the City's Homeowner Affidavit. An energy storage system permit requires a Master Electrician or a Homeowner Affidavit.
Fort Collins Utilities tells contractors they must be registered with Building Services as a specialized trade contractor to install solar PV in Fort Collins.

Fort Collins Utilities size limits for interconnection (not a building permit rule): customer-owned systems up to the larger of 12 kW-DC or 200% of average annual use; leased or third-party-owned systems up to the larger of 7.2 kW-DC or 120% of the home's average annual electric use.
The utility says not to begin installation before the interconnection application is approved.
Reroofing: if an existing solar PV system must be removed and reinstalled, the City asks for a separate solar reinstallation permit.

Battery location and spacing must comply with IRC Section R328 and the City's interpretation. The ESS section cites the 2021 edition while the same page says new building codes took effect on April 1, 2026, so confirm the edition with Building Services.

Battery-only projects: the Utilities contractor page says to obtain a General Alteration Permit from Building Services, while the City's permit page lists an Energy Storage System (ESS) permit type. Ask Building Services which permit applies.

Historic properties: all exterior work must be reviewed and approved before work begins. Email preservation@fortcollins.gov to begin Design Review. On sloped roofs that do not face the street, flush-mounted panels are allowed if they do not cover character-defining features and do not damage or remove historic features.
Plug-in or balcony solar: the utility says installation of portable-scale solar generation devices will not be allowed in the City of Fort Collins before January 1, 2027.

eligibility_constraints.notes: Size limits listed are Fort Collins Utilities interconnection limits, not building permit limits.

value.name: Solar PV (New Installation), residential
value.notes: The City splits it into a $29.75 Plan Check Fee, due when you apply, and a $55.25 Building Permit Fee, due when your permit is issued.

value.name: Solar PV Reinstallation
value.notes: For reinstalling existing panels in the same location, or replacing them with identical panels in the same location, with no system changes.

permit_fees.notes: Fees are as printed in the solar sections of the City's Building Permits page. The page prints no effective date next to them. Each solar section also lists sales tax, calculated on the total valuation of the project (materials and labor), with no dollar figure. Permits are not processed or reviewed until the Plan Check Fee, where one applies, has been paid. Remaining fees are due when your permit is issued.

value.name: 2026 Residential Solar Rebate
value.description: $300 per kW-DC of solar, up to a maximum incentive of $1,500. The minimum size is 0.5 kW, and 5 kW-DC of solar earns the maximum. The same table lists a maximum of $7,500 for a new system and $7,500 for adding to an existing system, which equals the solar maximum ($1,500) plus the battery maximum ($6,000). Amounts are based on the installed design and may be reduced if expected performance falls below optimal because of orientation or shading. In exchange for the incentive, you agree to sell all Renewable Energy Credits (RECs) from the system to Fort Collins Utilities for 20 years. The incentive table is labeled 2026 and prints no end date.
value.eligibility: The system must be sold and installed by a Participating Solar Contractor. It must be interconnected behind a residential solar meter on the Fort Collins Utilities electric distribution network. All equipment must be new, UL-listed and on the CEC approved equipment list. Do-it-yourself projects are allowed but are not eligible for rebates. A customer who already received a rebate on an existing solar installation is eligible for a second rebate for additional solar and battery storage at the same address.

value.name: Epic Loan (financing, not a rebate)
value.description: Fort Collins Utilities offers the Epic Loan to help finance home efficiency upgrades, including residential solar and battery storage. The page lists a maximum loan amount of $50,000 and interest rates as low as 5.25% APR.
value.eligibility: Customers working with contractors on the City's suspended contractor list are not eligible for Epic Loans. The page also lists a minimum FICO score of 640 and good payment history for 6 months on the Fort Collins Utilities account.
